title: Surface Structural Evolution of Air-Exposed Carbon-Coated LiFePO4 from Supercritical Hydrothermal Synthesis
content: LiFePO4 (LFP) batteries offer high energy density and stability, yet their performance is hindered by poor conductivity (∼10⁻⁹ S cm⁻¹) and an exceptionally slow lithium diffusion rate (∼10⁻¹⁴ to 10⁻¹⁵ cm² s⁻¹). The surface structure of LFP plays a critical role in regulating electron and ion transport, directly impacting performance, stability, and lifespan. It faces a constant struggle against unstable surface chemistry, whether from electrochemical cycling or air exposure during modification and storage. Among these threats, air exposure is a major culprit, causing pre-existing surface damage even before operation. This deterioration mechanism, distinct from electrochemical cycling-induced transformations, remains largely unexplored and demands thorough investigation.
